main_text.l: guine repleantur & quasi exsaturentur. Cons. vers.
42. hujus cantici.
Quandò dicit consumam tela mea, perpetuat
meta-phoram, ab arquitibus desumptam, qui à jaculando
non absistunt in bello, donec telum ultimum projece-
rint, atque pharetram planè evacuaverint: ita quoque
se actūrum statuit Deus cum Judæis (quippe omnibus
qualiumcunque suppliciorum & calamitatum telis iracun-
diæ suæ pharetram exhausturus) donec nullum vindictæ
genus reliquum sit, quod in hostes istos non effuderit.
Nota ergo telorum multitudinem, famem, pestilen-
tiam, hostiles cædes, bestiarum incursus, & quæ in s-
equentibus porrò numerantur: nec non omnium isto-
rum malorum immissionem[?], donec Deus penitus
per-fecerit vindictam suam, inculcari.
Vers. 24. Consumpti erunt fame. Junius exesos.
Coccejus ustos fame. Hi radicem Chaldaicam [illegible, ~3
letters] agnoscunt, quod verbum occurit. Dan. 3:19. atque
urere & succendere significat: atque ejus participium
in nostro textu occurrere autumant, ubi legimus [illegible, ~4
letters]. Nihilominus Doctissimus Capellus vocem [illegible, ~3 letters] potius
nomen esse quam participium vult, vertitque ardores
fa-mis, quod haud quaquam respuendum videtur. Pri-
mum itaque vindictæ divinæ telum ponitur fames, sæ-
pius in lege Dei inter plagas numerata, quâ Deus
ingratos puniret. Lev. 26:28.29. Deut. 28:22-24.
Durum telum necessitas, præsertim ad famem
increscens. Ezech. 5:16. Huic tribuuntur ardores. Thren.
5:10. Solet enim fames instar flammæ omnem succum
vegetum exhaurire, certamque mortem inferre,
dum vitales spiritus depascit, atque absumit. Malum
sanè horrendum, atque molestissimo sensu homines enecans,
& ferè ad rabiem redigens.

page.notes: Long s rendered as plain s throughout. "Vers." and "Cons." are read from the abbreviations "Verf." and "Conf." under the rule for long s. Two Hebrew words in the Chaldaic and Hebrew citations are not legible enough to copy and are marked illegible. "immissionem" is a doubtful reading of "imnuiffionem" and is marked [?]. A small asterisk stands in the left margin beside "fames" (line of "Primum itaque"); it is not a note reference and has no note text, so it is not transcribed. A small printer's bullet stands below the text near the centre, and a bullet also stands beside the catchword; neither is printed text.
